title: Untethered release-train adapter and launch cadence consolidation
creator: Marta Ruiz
description: Problem: Multiple product teams (runtime, console, API) run independent release trains that drift in cadence and blackout windows, causing last-minute capacity contention and duplicated cutover work. Goal: Create an "untethered" release-train adapter that lets teams keep preferred sprint rhythms while consolidating a single launch calendar, capacity reservation protocol, and cutover signal surface so cross-surface rollouts are predictable and low-risk. This ticket scopes product-level coordination (calendar + policy) and produces a lightweight adapter spec plus an operational playbook for upcoming Q2 launches.
tasks: Run stakeholder intake interviews with runtime, console, API leads (complete)
Draft adapter contract: signal schema, blackout semantics, preferred cadence mapping
Define capacity reservation tiers and burst lanes for Dedicated and Hosted customers
Prototype calendar UI wireframe and export APIs for automation
Align rollout gating criteria (latency SLOs, error budget, model-impact tests)
Publish playbook and run two shadow launches during Cycle 2026-W12
Collect telemetry hooks for post-launch retro and automated rollback triggers
acceptance_criteria: Adapter spec signed off by runtime, console, and API PMs
Calendar export API implemented with at least one consumer (release-engineering) using it
Two shadow launches completed with no customer-facing incidents
Ops playbook published in Confluence with runbook links and owners
Capacity reservation policy documented and integrated into launch request flow
risks: Teams may resist cadence changes leading to partial adoption
Capacity reservations could be overcommitted if teams inaccurately forecast traffic
Tooling gaps (calendar automation) could create manual overhead during early rollouts
Model-impacting runtime changes might require rollback semantics not yet codified
mitigations: Design the adapter to be non-blocking: teams opt-in gradually via feature flags
Require a minimal traffic estimate and a confidence band; Ops will enforce burst lanes
Deliver a simple CSV/ICS export as interim integration while automation is built
Define explicit health signals and a fast-fail rollback checklist in the playbook
